breakfast.name: Longganisa (Filipino Sausage)
breakfast.description: Filipino sweet sausage served with garlic fried rice and egg
instructions: Mix pork with garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, paprika, oregano
Pan fry until cooked through and caramelized
Serve with garlic fried rice and fried egg
breakfast.notes: The Filipino style is sweeter than other Asian sausages
breakfast.fun_fact: Longganisa is served daily in Filipino breakfast tables and is a national favorite

lunch.name: Adobo (Braised Chicken)
lunch.description: Filipino braised chicken in soy-vinegar sauce
instructions: Heat oil, sauté garlic until fragrant
Add chicken, brown on all sides
Add soy sauce, vinegar, water, bay leaves, pepper
Reduce heat, cover and simmer 35-40 minutes
lunch.notes: The balance of soy and vinegar is key
lunch.fun_fact: Adobo is the unofficial national dish of the Philippines and is served at every celebration

dinner.name: Kare-Kare (Peanut Stew)
dinner.description: Filipino peanut stew with meat and vegetables
instructions: Heat annatto oil, sauté onion and garlic
Mix peanut butter with broth, add to pot
Serve with shrimp paste on the side
dinner.fun_fact: Kare-Kare is a festive Filipino dish served at celebrations and special dinners

snacks.name: Lumpia (Spring Rolls)
snacks.description: Filipino fried spring rolls with meat and vegetables
instructions: Serve with sweet and sour sauce
snacks.notes: Filling must be cool before wrapping
snacks.fun_fact: Lumpia is the most popular Filipino appetizer and is served at every party

desserts.name: Halo-Halo (Mixed Dessert)
desserts.description: Filipino shaved ice dessert with beans, fruits, and condensed milk
instructions: Prepare all toppings: drain beans, beans, add to bowl
Layer half the ice in glass
Add layers of beans, corn, palm seeds
Top with leche flan pieces and fruit
Pour evaporated milk and condensed milk
Top with another piece of flan
desserts.notes: Must serve immediately before ice melts
desserts.fun_fact: Halo-Halo is the most iconic Filipino dessert and is served at every dessert shop

drinks.name: Buko Juice (Young Coconut)
drinks.description: Fresh young coconut juice straight from the fruit
instructions: Scrape soft flesh from shell if desired
drinks.fun_fact: Buko Juice is a refreshing Filipino drink sold by street vendors and is the national thirst quencher

drinks.name: Lambanog (Coconut Whiskey)
drinks.description: Filipino coconut spirit from Quezon, served ice-cold
instructions: Often chased with juice or water
drinks.fun_fact: Lambanog is called the 'Philippine counterpart to vodka' and has been produced for centuries
